expected_findings.validation_notes: Engine should emit one informational per include_file directive (or one consolidated informational naming all three paths). Per 14_DETECTION_ENGINE.md § 'Open issues', v1.0 does not resolve includes; the contract is that the user is told this so they can either (a) inline the includes for analysis or (b) provide the include allowlist when v2.0 supports include resolution.

validation_notes: Note: OSIPS-SEC-CFG-INCLUDE-UNRESOLVED is a synthetic rule_id used by this fixture as a stand-in. The actual rule_id may differ when the rule is authored — likely OSIPS-SEC-CFG-XXX in the config_hygiene family. Update this fixture once the rule is authored.

The engine must NOT silently pass on rules whose triggers might be in the included content. For example, TLS-001 must not fire (because we can't see tls.cfg), but the engine should report 'TLS-001 not evaluable: tls_mgm modparams may be in unresolved include' as a rules_skipped entry in diagnostics.

If the engine fires TLS-001 on this cfg as if the [default] domain has no verify_cert set (because the engine sees no verify_cert modparam in the parent file), that is a defect. The engine has incomplete information; firing on incomplete information is wrong.
Conversely, if the engine emits a clean report and lets the user believe the cfg is verified, that is also a defect. The user must know about the unresolved includes.
